boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Loras rituals and recurring practices, from bookend bell rings and a painted hillside to finals breakfast and Duhawk-wide celebrations.

cards.title: Ring In, Ring Out
cards.subtitle: First-year arrival and the final class share one bell
cards.notes: Ring the Victory Bell when you enroll, then return after your final senior class to mark the two ends of a Loras education.
cards.short_summary: The same historic bell welcomes first-year students and sends seniors onward.
cards.evidence_claim: Loras states that first-year students ring the Victory Bell upon enrolling and seniors ring it after their last class; school legend connects the bell to Mount St. Bernard’s Seminary.
cards.source_title: Student Clubs & Organizations | Get Involved | Loras College
cards.access_notes: Participation is tied to enrollment for first-year students and completion of the last class for seniors.

cards.title: Arrive Before the Crowd
cards.subtitle: New Duhawks begin campus life together
cards.notes: Move in with the incoming class before returning students arrive, then use the scheduled activities to learn campus and meet classmates.
cards.short_summary: A shared early move-in turns the incoming class’s first days into a collective launch.
cards.evidence_claim: Loras describes Launch into Loras as an experience in which new students move in before returning students and join orientation, relationship-building, and recreational activities.
cards.source_title: Student Clubs & Organizations | Get Involved | Loras College
cards.access_notes: Intended for students beginning their Loras experience; follow the college’s incoming-student schedule.

cards.title: Let Faculty Serve Finals Breakfast
cards.subtitle: A 9 p.m. study-break ritual with breakfast food
cards.notes: Pause finals work from 9 to 10 p.m. for breakfast food and watch familiar faculty and staff take their turns serving at the stations.
cards.short_summary: Finals pressure gives way to a one-hour breakfast served by campus employees.
cards.evidence_claim: Loras documents Late Night Cafe as a finals-stress break from 9 to 10 p.m. featuring breakfast food and faculty and staff serving at the stations.
cards.source_title: Student Clubs & Organizations | Get Involved | Loras College
cards.access_notes: The official page specifies a current event time of 9–10 p.m.; consult the campus event schedule for the date and location.

cards.title: Rewrite the Hillside for Homecoming
cards.subtitle: An October message painted before alumni return
cards.notes: Look for the October painting session before Homecoming and help create the large community message only through the organized campus activity.
cards.short_summary: Students transform Loras’s prominent hill into a temporary Homecoming message.
cards.evidence_claim: Loras says students paint the hill with a community message every October before Homecoming and that photographs document the tradition from the early 1950s.
cards.source_title: Student Clubs & Organizations | Get Involved | Loras College
cards.access_notes: Seasonal October activity held before Homecoming; participate only through the college-organized event.

cards.title: Trade the Hill’s Paint for Snow
cards.subtitle: The Homecoming canvas becomes a winter sled run
cards.notes: Wait for suitable winter conditions, bring a purpose-made sled, and follow posted campus guidance rather than reviving the former cafeteria-tray custom.
cards.short_summary: The same campus slope known for its painted message becomes a winter recreation spot.
cards.evidence_claim: Loras documents that students and local families enjoy sledding down the hill in winter and notes that cafeteria trays were used in the not-so-distant past.
cards.source_title: Student Clubs & Organizations | Get Involved | Loras College
cards.access_notes: Weather-dependent outdoor activity; use a proper sled and comply with current campus conditions and safety guidance.

cards.title: Turn the Day Purple and Gold
cards.subtitle: A worldwide March gathering of Duhawk support
cards.notes: Wear purple and gold, join a campus or community activity, and share a Loras memory; donating is one option, not the only way to participate.
cards.short_summary: Students, alumni, families, and friends connect worldwide during a 24-hour Loras celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Loras calls Duhawk Day an annual signature tradition launched in 2013; participants wear purple and gold, share memories, and join digital and in-person activities during the 24-hour event.
cards.source_title: Loras Community Rallies for Duhawk Day, Surpassing 2,000 Donors for Sixth Consecutive Year | Loras College
cards.access_notes: Annual March event with digital and in-person participation; consult the current Duhawk Day program for scheduled activities.

cards.title: Put Student Work on Display
cards.subtitle: Presentations, posters, and films share one academic stage
cards.notes: Plan to present or attend across formats—talks, poster sessions, and the film festival—to see what other Duhawks have created and studied.
cards.short_summary: A campus-wide showcase gives scholarly work a celebratory public forum.
cards.evidence_claim: Loras states that the Legacy Symposium showcases student academic achievements through presentations, poster sessions, and a film festival.
cards.source_title: Student Clubs & Organizations | Get Involved | Loras College
cards.access_notes: Follow the current symposium program for presentation eligibility, event locations, and attendance details.

cards.title: Keep a 1910 Stage Tradition Moving
cards.subtitle: Students of every major continue the Loras Players story
cards.notes: Audition, join a production crew, or attend a performance to take part in a student theatre program that Loras traces continuously to 1910.
cards.short_summary: Each new production extends a student theatre lineage more than a century old.
cards.evidence_claim: Loras states that the Loras Players were established in 1910 and remain a continuously operating, multidisciplinary student theatre troupe open to students of all majors.
cards.source_title: Student Clubs & Organizations | Get Involved | Loras College
cards.access_notes: Production participation is for Loras students; performance access and any ticket requirements depend on the current season.

cards.entity_name: Christ the King Chapel Bell Ringing
cards.title: Hear the Duhawk Fight Song from the Chapel
cards.subtitle: Restored bells mark hours, prayer, seasons, and school spirit
cards.notes: Listen near Christ the King Chapel at noon for the Angelus or during daytime hourly ringing; seasonal music and the fight song may also sound.
cards.short_summary: A restored campus soundscape combines Catholic observance with distinctly Duhawk music.
cards.evidence_claim: Loras reports that the restored Christ the King Chapel bells ring hourly from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., sound the Angelus at noon, and can play seasonal selections and the Duhawk Fight Song.
cards.source_title: Christ the King Bells Ring Again at Loras College | Loras College
cards.access_notes: The published schedule is hourly from 9 a.m.–6 p.m., with the Angelus at noon; the bells are heard from public campus areas.

cards.title: Come Home as a Duhawk
cards.subtitle: Reunions and campus events reconnect generations
cards.notes: Build a weekend around your class reunion, an athletic event, or a campus program, checking the official schedule because registration varies by activity.
cards.short_summary: Homecoming brings alumni, families, and friends back into the rhythms of campus life.
cards.evidence_claim: Loras says thousands of alumni, family members, and friends return each year for Homecoming reunions, athletic competitions, panels, networking, tailgating, and other events.
cards.source_title: Loras College Homecoming | Alumni & Friends | Duhawk Pride
cards.access_notes: Annual scheduled weekend; some activities require advance registration, so use the official Homecoming event list.
